newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-WEEKEND FRENCH FIRST DIVISION PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND FRENCH FIRST DIVISION PROGRAMME.

text.p: French first division matches this weekend (league positions in brackets):

Bastia's Anton Drobnjak, first division joint top scorer, returns from World Cup action with Yugoslavia. Monaco are still without injured Belgian Enzo Scifo, Swiss Marco Grassi and France defender Eric Di Meco and suspended midfielder Lilian Martin, but Scot John Collins is back from World Cup duty.

The champions, gearing up for the crucial European Champions' League clash at home to Grasshopper Zurich next week, are without striker Lilian Laslandes who has back trouble. Midfielder Sabri Lamouchi, who twisted an ankle playing for France against Turkey on Wednesday, is doubtful. In his absence Moussa Saib becomes the first Algerian to captain a French first division side. Guinea striker Aboubacar Camara is back for Lens.

Nice will be without suspended Milinkovic and injured Italian Roberto Onorati as they look to bounce back from their 7-0 defeat at Nantes. Montpellier expect to be strengthened by the return from injury of former French international Franck Sauzee, goalkeeper Bruno Martini and Argentine Jose Luis Villarreal.

Young striker Djezon Boutoille could return for Lille. Nantes, 7-0 winners at home to Nice last Saturday, are flying in teenage goalkeeper Mickael Landreau, unbeaten in his first two first division matches, from international duty with France's juniors in Sweden.

Metz, a serious threat to PSG's unbeaten record, have France winger Robert Pires suspended, but Cameroon's Rigobert Song back from African Nations Cup duty. Brazil's Rai is available for the league leaders after injury, but Alain Roche, who pulled out of France's midweek friendly against Turkey with an injury, and fellow defender Bruno N'Gotty are doubtful.

Jean-Pierre Papin, who missed the home defeat to Strasbourg and the 0-0 draw at Caen, returns after a private trip to the U.S. to face bottom club Nancy, but former PSG defender Patrick Colleter is suspended. Northern Ireland's Phil Gray is back for winless Nancy.
Striker Roger Boli is fit again for selection for Le Havre, but Lyon's Franck Gava, who made his France debut as a substitute in midweek, is suspended.

Red card problems mean Marseille must again reshuffle the pack in defence. Hamada Jambay, sent off at Strasbourg last weekend, is suspended, while Italian Ivan Franceschini, who missed that match through suspension, is available again. They also welcome back internationals absent last Sunday -- German goalkeeper Andreas Koepke, Ireland striker Tony Cascarino and Tunisia's Medhi Ben Slimane. Caen are still looking for their first win.

Strasbourg defender Jan Suchoparek, who missed the win over Marseille on Sunday because of the Czech Republic's World Cup qualifier against Spain, is back. Guingamp's internationals including Liberian Christopher Wreh and Erik Assaduryan, who scored in Armenia's shock win in Northern Ireland last Saturday, are also available.

Rennes will be glad of the extra day's preparation after missing half their squad through injury or international duty during the week. Cannes's three French under-21 internationals, Romain Ferrier, Mickael Marsiglia and Lilian Compan, have all returned carrying injuries and are doubtful.
